Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window once again proved to be exceptionally busy, with some huge names making big-money moves all the way up to Deadline Day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: Infantino attends Caribbean Football Union meeting despite objection from CONCACAF
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has reportedly irked CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani after attending a recent Caribbean Football Union (CFU) meeting, despite being asked to stay away. Reports said several Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF) members were upset after Infantino allegedly used the meeting to announce FIFA-funded development projects worth millions of dollars, some of which had been delayed for months. Montagliani had written to Infantino urging him “in the name of football to reconsider your attendance,” arguing that his presence would overshadow the regional Under-14 tournament taking place alongside the meeting.

news.title: From Baghdad to Toronto: What awaits Arab fans at the 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: TORONTO: As the FIFA World Cup 2026 gets underway across North America, thousands of Arab football fans are preparing to follow Iraq’s journey on football’s biggest stage. For many, Toronto could become one of the tournament’s most welcoming destinations. news.title: Football Legends and the Power of World Cup Nostalgia
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup has come to an end, and there is good reason people are talking about what a success it was. Revenues are estimated to be between USD 13.5 billion and USD 15 billion for the entire 2023–2026 cycle, surpassing the USD 11 billion expectation for this period. Another of the hottest talking points was the “Americanization” of the tournament featuring the “4 quarters” due to controversial hydration breaks, the halftime show at the final, and shots of celebrities in the stands during the broadcast, all typical of U.S. sports. In addition to the FIFA president, who appeared in broadcasts during the 9th minute of every match, the legends stole the spotlight.

news.title: ‘In my heart until I die’: Argentina says a tearful thank you to Lionel Messi
news.lede: The Argentinian’s decision to quit international football was met by an outpouring of affection from the country he led to World Cup glory in 2022. Anyone who was present at Lionel Scaloni’s press conference immediately after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in New Jersey on 19 July and saw his tears, the sobs which prevented him from speaking while he got up and walked out, could tell this was a man weeping not because of defeat in a single match but because he was fully aware that what that particular group of men had been through for the past eight years had come to an end.
